explanation.b: The techniques are mitigations that make checking faster without replacing it, so what would hurt if wrong is still checked against the source (module 5, page 2).
explanation.e: The techniques are mitigations that make checking faster without replacing it, so what would hurt if wrong is still checked against the source (module 5, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The documentation's own techniques turn some of this into a prompt", which is a request to the model and not a check in code.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "confidence is not evidence".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the documentation says they "don't eliminate them entirely".

quizzes.stem: An HR assistant uploads a group photo from a company event and asks Claude to name each person pictured for a directory. What should the team expect?

options.a: Names looked up from the staff files after Claude checks each face against them
options.b: Accurate names for everyone whose face is clear, with a note of uncertainty
options.c: Approximate names, with each face marked by pixel coordinates
options.d: A refusal to identify them, so labels come from a roster or the people

explanation.d: Claude cannot be used to name people in images and refuses to (module 4, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because what training gives excludes "Access to your files, systems or today's date".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Claude cannot be used to name people in images, and refuses to".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Coordinates and localisation outputs are approximate", and the refusal still applies.

quizzes.stem: Claude works through a multi-step pricing calculation and gives a confident chain of steps ending in a total. What should decide whether the total is trusted?

options.a: The model's own statement that it re-checked each step it took
options.b: A rerun of the arithmetic in code, compared with the stated figure
options.c: A higher thinking setting for the same calculation
options.d: The length and detail of the steps shown to the reader

explanation.b: Reasoning that decides something important needs an independent check, and code that redoes the arithmetic is one (module 4, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Self-reported confidence is not a measure of accuracy".
explanation.c: Ruled out because more thinking is still the same reasoning, and a decisive step "needs a check that does not come from the same reasoning".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A confident chain of steps can contain a wrong step that makes everything after it wrong".

quizzes.stem: A retailer asks Claude to return pixel coordinates of price tags in shelf photos and crops each photo automatically. Some crops miss the tags by a few pixels. Which limit explains it?

options.a: Claude reads only the text printed in images, so positions are pure guesses
options.b: Coordinates come back exact, so the cropping script is at fault
options.c: Spatial answers are approximate, so each cut-out needs a margin or a check
options.d: Object counts are approximate, so some crops land on the wrong tag

explanation.c: The vision page lists spatial reasoning among its limits, so pixel positions from a photo need a margin or a check (module 4, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Claude reads images and PDFs", and the page calls positions approximate, not guesses.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Coordinates and localisation outputs are approximate", so they are not exact.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the counting limit, "can give approximate counts of objects in an image", concerns how many tags there are, while these crops miss by a few pixels.

quizzes.stem: A benefits chatbot answers from the company handbook, but some replies add rules borrowed from how other employers work. Which prompt instruction targets this?

options.a: Run each question three times and keep the answer that repeats most often
options.b: Give it the role of an HR director with many years of experience
options.c: Ask it to state how sure it is about each rule that it gives
options.d: Tell it to rely solely on the supplied texts, ignoring its training

explanation.d: Restricting knowledge tells the model to use only the provided documents, not its general knowledge (module 1, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Comparing detects the variation; it does not remove it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A role is a request, not a credential".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Self-reported confidence is not a measure of accuracy".

quizzes.stem: A student uses Claude to find sources for an essay and pastes three citations into the bibliography, one of which does not exist. Which two habits would have prevented it? (Select two.)

options.a: Verify every fact that enters graded work
options.b: Switch to a larger model for the source search
options.c: Proofread the essay's tone and grammar with care
options.d: Confirm each reference in a library or database
options.e: Ask Claude if the sources it gave are real

explanation.a: A student checks every fact and citation that goes into graded work, because a hallucination includes "an invented citation, a function that does not exist" (module 9, page 1).
explanation.d: A student checks every fact and citation that goes into graded work, because a hallucination includes "an invented citation, a function that does not exist" (module 9, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because the mechanism holds for any model: "a plausible-looking fact is a likely continuation whether or not it is true".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Readers check tone and grammar, which are visible, and skip figures and citations".
explanation.e: Ruled out because "Self-reported confidence is not a measure of accuracy".

quizzes.stem: A freelance writer uses Claude to draft a short story opening and wants to be sure it is safe to publish under their own name. Which check does the course name for creative work?

options.a: Whether a disclosure line can be skipped for pieces this short
options.b: Whether it is too close to another author's existing piece
options.c: Whether the opening reads smoothly enough to publish as is
options.d: Whether Claude's reply says that the opening is original

explanation.b: For creative work the checks start with originality, whether the piece echoes someone's existing work (module 9, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Disclosure matters more here than in many fields".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page names "Treating a fluent first draft as finished work" as a trap.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Self-reported confidence is not a measure of accuracy".

quizzes.stem: A team has no benchmark yet and must pick a first model for a broad mix of ordinary workloads, with no tight cost or latency limit. Which starting point does the models overview advise?

options.a: Begin with Claude Haiku 4.5, then move up a tier whenever it fails
options.b: Begin with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and add tests once a problem shows
options.c: Begin with Claude Fable 5.1, then move down a tier to save cost
options.d: Begin with Claude Opus 5.5, and try Fable 5.1 if evals fall short

explanation.d: The overview's default advice is to start with Claude Opus 5.5 for most workloads and use Claude Fable 5.1 when evals at higher effort still fall short (module 3, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because starting with the fast tier is "Suited to prototyping, tight latency, cost sensitivity", and the team has none of these.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Having a good evaluation set is the most important step".
explanation.c: Ruled out because putting ordinary workloads on the top tier is the trap where "It raises cost and latency on work that does not need it".

quizzes.stem: A designer uses Firefox and a phone, and asks whether Claude in Chrome can be installed there. Which two statements does the course support? (Select two.)

options.a: It is a side panel in a single browser
options.b: It is offered on the free plan too
options.c: It is a tab inside the Claude web app
options.d: It runs as a desktop extension on any device
options.e: Other browsers and mobile are excluded

explanation.a: Claude in Chrome is an extension in the Chrome side panel on the paid plans, and "It is not supported on other Chromium browsers or on mobile" (module 8, page 2).
explanation.e: Claude in Chrome is an extension in the Chrome side panel on the paid plans, and "It is not supported on other Chromium browsers or on mobile" (module 8, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because the extension is offered "on the paid plans (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise)".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Claude in Chrome is a browser extension, in the Chrome side panel", not a page of the web app.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Desktop extensions are for the desktop app only".

quizzes.stem: A start-up wants Claude in its mobile app, keeping chat history in its own database and calling its own tools. Which surface fits?

options.a: Claude Code, the terminal agent for everyday software work
options.b: A Project in the apps, with its own shared files and notes
options.c: Managed agents, hosted and run by the provider
options.d: The Messages API, with the loop and the state written by hand

explanation.d: A product needing Claude inside its own screens uses the Messages API (module 3, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because that row is for "A developer wants help changing a codebase".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the apps row reads "Instructions and uploads, not code".
explanation.c: Ruled out because that row is for "A job runs for hours and should not tie up your servers".

quizzes.stem: A developer team wants a bespoke agent that edits files and runs commands the way Claude Code does, but driven from its own program with its own permission rules. Which surface fits?

options.a: The SDK, which ships the same engine as a library
options.b: Claude Code itself, used as a ready-made tool
options.c: Managed agents, hosted and run by the provider
options.d: The Messages API, called directly with a loop

explanation.a: The Agent SDK lets you build your own agents powered by Claude Code's tools and capabilities, with full control over orchestration, tool access and permissions (module 3, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because that row is for "A developer wants help changing a codebase".
explanation.c: Ruled out because that row is for "A job runs for hours and should not tie up your servers".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the API row says "Direct access to the model; your own loop, tools and state".

quizzes.stem: A company on a Pro plan wants Claude Tag in its Slack workspace. What should the company be told?

options.a: It works on any plan, but only where zero data retention is enabled
options.b: It needs a Team or Enterprise subscription, on Anthropic's own service
options.c: It is offered on every paid plan, including Pro and Max, for any workspace
options.d: It is offered through cloud platforms such as Bedrock as well as directly

explanation.b: Claude Tag is available on Team and Enterprise plans only, on Anthropic's own service, and not for organisations with zero data retention or customer-managed encryption (module 8, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because it is "not for organisations with zero data retention or customer-managed encryption, because it stores channel memory and session transcripts".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says it is "available on Team and Enterprise plans only".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says it runs "on Anthropic's own service".

quizzes.stem: A free-plan user wants to hand Cowork a folder on their computer. What must they have before Cowork can work in it?

options.a: A terminal and the command-line tool installed on the computer
options.b: A Pro plan and Cowork open in the web app in a browser
options.c: A paid subscription and the open, connected desktop app
options.d: The free plan and the desktop app, with the folder connected

explanation.c: Cowork needs a paid plan, and local file access needs the desktop app for macOS or Windows to be open and connected (module 8, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "There is no terminal".
explanation.b: Ruled out because web access does not reach local files, which "need the Claude desktop app for macOS or Windows to be open and connected".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Cowork needs a paid plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise)".

quizzes.stem: A manager asks Claude for a two-sentence reply to a colleague and then for a reusable 40-line status dashboard for the team. Which pair of outputs does the help centre's rule produce?

options.a: The reply inline, the dashboard as raw structured data
options.b: Both as artifacts, opened in a side panel for the manager
options.c: The brief one in chat, the larger one as an artifact
options.d: Both inline, kept in the chat thread as plain text

explanation.c: A short answer stays inline, and significant, self-contained, reusable content becomes an artifact (module 7, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Data that another program will read is structured data", and the dashboard is for the team to open.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A short answer stays inline in the chat".
explanation.d: Ruled out because artifacts include "documents, code, web pages, images and diagrams, dashboards and interactive tools".

quizzes.stem: An agent updated customer records and sent emails by itself for a month. Some records are now wrong, a few emails reached the wrong clients, and nobody can say which changes it made. Which arrangement, in place from the start, would have caught this?

options.a: A fixed scope, a review before anything lands, and a log of its work
options.b: A colleague's login, broad access, and its work filed under their name
options.c: A fixed scope, free action within it, and a weekly summary of its work
options.d: A fixed scope, a close watch in week one, and no logging after that

explanation.a: The agent is treated like a new colleague with limited access: a defined scope, a review before consequences and a record (module 5, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because an agent gets "accounts of its own, with the narrowest role that covers the work".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the habit needs "a review before consequences", not after them.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the agent needs "a record of what happened" for as long as it acts.

quizzes.stem: An office manager considers letting Claude clear old customer files from a shared drive automatically each night. Which reason from the delegation guidance argues against handing this step over?

options.a: Claude cannot delete files, so the clean-up is beyond what it can do
options.b: A mistake there would be hard to undo once the deletion had run
options.c: A nightly job needs the computer awake, so the run would stall
options.d: Customer files are confidential, so an AI tool may not open them

explanation.b: A step stays with a person or code when a mistake would be hard to reverse (module 5, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Claude can read, write and permanently delete files in the folders you connect".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a recurring task "does not need your computer awake or the desktop app open".
explanation.d: Ruled out because confidential data goes "Only in approved tools, with a need to know", which allows an approved tool.

quizzes.stem: A manager sets a recurring Cowork task for the early morning and wants it to run while the laptop is shut and the desktop app is closed. Which two statements does the page support? (Select two.)

options.a: No awake computer is needed at that hour
options.b: Someone must approve each run as it starts
options.c: It needs the desktop app open and connected
options.d: It waits until the laptop is restarted
options.e: Anthropic's own servers handle the job

explanation.a: A recurring task set with /schedule "runs in the cloud, so it does not need your computer awake or the desktop app open" (module 8, page 1).
explanation.e: A recurring task set with /schedule "runs in the cloud, so it does not need your computer awake or the desktop app open" (module 8, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Scheduled tasks run while you are away", with nobody there to approve each run.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Tasks run in the cloud on Anthropic's servers", not through the desktop app.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "sessions can continue when your computer is offline".

quizzes.stem: A ceramic artist asks how to bring Claude into the practice before it touches any part of the work. Which approach fits the creative-work course?

options.a: Full use from the start, dropped later wherever it harms the style
options.b: Use at every stage of the work, from sketch to final glaze
options.c: Use it first on the idea and the voice, where the style is set
options.d: None at first, then add it to a task only if both lenses favour it

explanation.d: The course recommends a deliberate starting point of no AI, adding it only where analysis says it earns its place (module 9, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because full use from the start hands over the voice, and "For a maker the distinctive voice is the product".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a maker delegates only "the parts of the production that do not carry the maker's voice".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the maker keeps "the idea, the voice, the final choices and the signature".

quizzes.stem: A consultant signs off an AI-drafted report under their own name and tells the client an assistant helped write it. Which competency of Anthropic's four-part fluency framework did they exercise?

options.a: Description: have I said what I want so the job can be done and judged?
options.b: Diligence: will I stand behind this and say what the AI did?
options.c: Discernment: is what came back accurate, complete, fair and fit for its reader?
options.d: Delegation: which parts of this job go to the AI and which stay with me?

explanation.b: Owning the result and being honest about the AI's part is Diligence: will I stand behind this, tell people honestly what Claude did and have I protected the data (module 9, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because that question belongs to the habit of describing: "Have I said what I want, so the job can be done and judged?"
explanation.c: Ruled out because the table gives that question as "Is what came back accurate, complete, fair and fit for its reader?" for the habit of judging.
explanation.d: Ruled out because that question belongs to deciding what to hand over: "Which parts of this job go to Claude, and which stay with me?"

quizzes.stem: An analyst wants help gathering details from a vendor's trusted support portal and filing a ticket there, with a say before any step goes through. Which tool and setting fit?

options.a: Claude in Chrome with manual approval on each action
options.b: Claude in Chrome on automatic approval, screening each action
options.c: Cowork in Auto approval, screening each action itself
options.d: Research mode with web search on for all sites

explanation.a: A step-by-step task on a trusted live site, with a person confirming each step, suits Claude in Chrome in Manually approve mode (module 8, page 3).
explanation.b: Ruled out because in that mode "Claude keeps working and reviews each action for safety" instead of waiting for the analyst.
explanation.c: Ruled out because Auto checks each action "but it still runs on its own", so the analyst has no say before a step.
explanation.d: Ruled out because Research is for when "the question is open and broad", not for filling in a form on a site.

quizzes.stem: A manager has run the same competitor summary in plain chat every week for two months, retyping the rules and re-uploading the files, and still corrects each result by hand. What does the course suggest?

options.a: Switch to Claude in Chrome to have the web pages reread each week
options.b: Keep using plain chat for the weekly job as before
options.c: Put the routine in a Project or a skill of its own
options.d: Move to Cowork and let it run the weekly job on a schedule

explanation.c: Work that repeats with the same rules and files has outgrown a one-off chat, and a Project or a skill holds those rules for every run (module 8, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because Chrome is for "A step-by-step task on a website you trust".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says to "revisit it when the work changes".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Only once the output is reliably right is a weekly schedule added".

quizzes.stem: A lecturer asks Claude to draft a marking rubric and then to grade the pupils' essays against it, and records the grades. What stays with the lecturer under the course's guidance?

options.a: Only the recording, once Claude has marked each essay
options.b: The final signature, once Claude has produced each mark for the class
options.c: The first draft of the rubric, with the grading handed over
options.d: Judging each paper, with the AI's scores held only as suggestions

explanation.d: Judging student work and consequential decisions stays with the educator (module 9, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the usage policy treats "academic testing and admissions as a high-risk use needing human review".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the educator "Owns: what students are taught, how they are assessed and the fairness of grades", which a signature on Claude's marks does not give.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the educator delegates "draft lesson plans, example problems at several levels, rubric first drafts".

quizzes.stem: A project lead tags Claude in a channel thread to compile a report, then closes Slack for the evening. A colleague adds a correction as a later message. Which two statements describe what happens? (Select two.)

options.a: Replies posted afterwards are followed
options.b: It reads only the post that carried the tag
options.c: The finished report reaches the lead alone
options.d: It works through the lead's own claude.ai account
options.e: The work carries on in the cloud

explanation.a: Tasks run in the cloud, "Claude keeps working after you close Slack", and once in a thread it follows every reply (module 8, page 2).
explanation.e: Tasks run in the cloud, "Claude keeps working after you close Slack", and once in a thread it follows every reply (module 8, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because it reads "the thread it was tagged in (including earlier messages when mentioned mid-thread)" and not only the tagged post.
explanation.c: Ruled out because in a channel the result is seen by "Everyone in the channel, including Claude's checklist and results".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a channel uses "What an admin set up for that channel; everyone there gets the same access".

quizzes.stem: A new team member wants Claude to produce the entire quarterly customer review, from data pull to final slides, on their first day. What does the delegation guidance suggest?

options.a: Hand over the whole review once the first draft reads well
options.b: Hand over one written section and judge it before the next
options.c: Hand over the data pull first, the slowest part of the job
options.d: Hand over everything but ask for a confidence note at the end

explanation.b: Decide how much to hand over at once: a small, clear step with a visible result is easier to judge, so start narrow and widen (module 5, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A good draft does not show the figures were right".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the figures need "Exact numbers, authoritative source" from code or an analyst.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Self-reported confidence is not a measure of accuracy".

quizzes.stem: An operations lead wants to package the team's meeting-notes format so that Claude applies it whenever relevant, and has no programmer available. What is needed?

options.a: A saved prompt that each person pastes in at the start of a chat
options.b: A zipped folder with the rules written in Markdown, uploaded as a skill
options.c: A connector to the notes folder with write access for the assistant
options.d: A plugin built by a partner company for note-taking and shared with the team

explanation.b: A simple custom skill needs no code: Markdown instructions in the required folder structure, zipped and uploaded (module 7, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because a pasted prompt depends on someone remembering it, while with skills "Claude reviews which skills are available, loads the relevant ones and applies them".
explanation.c: Ruled out because connectors "let Claude access your apps and services, retrieve your data and take actions", which reaches data and does not package a format.
explanation.d: Ruled out because partner skills are "From other companies, built to work with their connectors".

quizzes.stem: A team builds a Project knowledge base from a colleague's email recap of a policy, an unsigned draft and a blurry photocopy with missing pages. Which principle did they ignore?

options.a: Judge the material first, preferring approved primary text
options.b: Remove superseded versions from the knowledge base
options.c: Name an owner and a review date for each file
options.d: Cite the source in each answer given to a reader of the Project

explanation.a: Quality in is quality out: prefer final approved text, primary documents and short clean files (module 7, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Two versions of one document side by side invite Claude to quote either", and the stem lists no duplicates.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "nothing alerts you when a file goes stale", which is about upkeep and not about the quality of what goes in.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a citation shows where an answer came from, not that the source is right".

quizzes.stem: A team wants Claude to work with an application installed on one employee's laptop, which has no web address. Which shape fits?

options.a: A skill that bundles the application's instructions for Claude to load
options.b: A Project holding an export of the application's data as knowledge
options.c: A desktop extension, which hosts its endpoint on that same computer
options.d: A remote connector, which reaches an MCP server from Anthropic's cloud

explanation.c: Desktop extensions are for the desktop app only and run a server locally, while remote connectors reach a server from Anthropic's cloud (module 7, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because skills are "folders of instructions, scripts and resources that Claude loads dynamically".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "an uploaded file is a copy as of the day you uploaded it", not a link to the application.
explanation.d: Ruled out because for a remote connector "the server must be reachable on the public internet".

quizzes.stem: A power user has connected twelve connectors and notices conversations feel crowded with tool lists. Which two statements fit the help centre's suggestion? (Select two.)

options.a: The choice is made at sign-in, when the scopes are approved
options.b: The loading mode decides what each tool may do
options.c: On demand is the default that suits most people
options.d: Choose On demand through the plus menu or the slash command
options.e: Ten or more is the point where it pays off

explanation.d: The page suggests On demand "when you have ten or more connectors", a choice made in the plus menu or the slash command (module 7, page 3).
explanation.e: The page suggests On demand "when you have ten or more connectors", a choice made in the plus menu or the slash command (module 7, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page puts the choice in the chat, where "you can choose how connector tools are loaded".
explanation.b: Ruled out because what tools may do is a separate setting: "Owners can set what the tools may do".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The default Auto mode suits most people".

quizzes.stem: A team's Project holds a pricing file uploaded a year ago, and its answers have drifted out of date unnoticed. Which practice would have prevented it?

options.a: Telling Claude in the instructions to flag old files whenever it notices them
options.b: Naming an accountable person for each source and fixing a recurring check
options.c: Uploading the file again whenever somebody happens to remember to do it
options.d: Keeping every earlier version in the Project, with a date in each name

explanation.b: Each source needs an owner and a review date, because nothing alerts you when a file goes stale (module 7, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "nothing alerts you when a file goes stale".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a stale file should be "a missed appointment, not a surprise".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Old and new documents side by side give Claude two sources to quote".

quizzes.stem: An analyst sets a formatting convention in the Excel add-in's instructions, then finds the Word add-in ignores it. Why?

options.a: Macros are unsupported, so a formatting rule cannot run in Word
options.b: Cross-app work is off, so the rule cannot pass into Word
options.c: Each app keeps its own rules, so this one never travelled over
options.d: The rule held only for the conversation where it was first set

explanation.c: Instructions are set per add-in and do not carry from Excel into Word or PowerPoint (module 8, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the rule is an instruction and not a macro, and "Instructions are set per add-in, in its settings".
explanation.b: Ruled out because cross-app work concerns files, so that "one conversation can read an Excel model and write a Word memo or a slide".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a convention set there "applies to every Excel conversation".

quizzes.stem: A paid-plan Project with a large knowledge base reaches its context limit and keeps working, but some replies now repeat garbled lines from a thick scanned file. What explains this?

options.a: It retrieves the relevant passages, so a muddled source shapes the output
options.b: It drops the oldest files first, so the scan is all that is left to quote
options.c: It condenses every file into a summary, so the scan's errors carry over
options.d: It keeps the whole base in the window, so the scan's bad pages dominate

explanation.a: Near the limit the paid plans switch on retrieval of the relevant parts, and a retrieved passage is only as good as its source (module 7, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A big knowledge base is possible" under that mode, so files are not dropped.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page describes "retrieval of the relevant parts", not a summary of every file.
explanation.d: Ruled out because when "a Project approaches the context limit Claude enables RAG mode" instead of holding everything in view.

quizzes.stem: A freelancer on a Pro plan, who has never changed a privacy setting, asks when Anthropic would use their chats to improve Claude. Which answer fits?

options.a: Only for incognito chats, which feed improvements to the models
options.b: Only if they opt in, or a conversation gets flagged for review
options.c: Only for chats they share with others or export to a file
options.d: Only for content brought in through a connector or an upload

explanation.b: Consumer chats are used only if the user allows it in privacy settings, or if a conversation is flagged (module 10, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Incognito chats are not used to improve Claude".
explanation.c: Ruled out because chats are used "only if you choose to allow it in your privacy settings", whether shared or not.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Raw content fetched through a connector is excluded unless you copy it into the chat".

quizzes.stem: A user sets Claude in Chrome to its least restrictive approval mode to save clicks while browsing a bank site. Which two statements does the page support? (Select two.)

options.a: It still pauses before each step on a bank page
options.b: It is advised for frequent sites like a bank
options.c: It is meant only for cases of complete trust
options.d: Nothing reviews the actions it takes there
options.e: Purchases then go through on a trusted site

explanation.c: Skip all approvals means nothing checks the actions, so it is for complete trust only, and the habit is "do not manage financial accounts, legal documents or medical information through it" (module 8, page 2).
explanation.d: Skip all approvals means nothing checks the actions, so it is for complete trust only, and the habit is "do not manage financial accounts, legal documents or medical information through it" (module 8, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because in that mode "Claude does not pause and nothing checks its actions".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the habit is to "prefer Manually approve for anything that matters".
explanation.e: Ruled out because "Making purchases or financial transactions" is prohibited regardless of permission mode.

quizzes.stem: A manager wants to paste an unreleased financial forecast into a chat tool that the company has sanctioned. Which rule fits?

options.a: Ask Claude to forget the forecast afterwards, which satisfies the rule
options.b: Treat it as internal, so any approved tool may receive it
options.c: Treat it as regulated, shared only with the owner's written consent
options.d: Treat it as confidential, shared only with those who need to know

explanation.d: Confidential data goes only in approved tools, with a need to know and often with identifiers removed (module 10, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "An instruction to forget is not a control".
explanation.b: Ruled out because confidential examples are "Contracts, unreleased financials, customer lists".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the regulated class holds "Health records, payment-card data, government IDs, personal data under GDPR".

quizzes.stem: A security lead wants Claude in chat and Cowork to stop reaching the open web for everyone, without disabling the apps. Which control do the pages describe?

options.a: An owner switch that turns search off across the organisation
options.b: A sites allowlist in the browser extension, which also covers chat and Cowork
options.c: A retention setting that limits how long fetched pages are kept
options.d: A per-user prompt telling Claude not to use the internet

explanation.a: Owners can turn web search off for chat and Cowork (module 10, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Claude in Chrome sites can be allow-listed or blocklisted".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the table lists "Retention settings, including custom retention or zero data retention for Enterprise agreements" for how long data is kept, not for where the web can reach.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A prompt is a request, not a guarantee".

quizzes.stem: An assistant asks a user to confirm "Send this email to everyone on the list?" while the user works through a long task and presses Allow without a glance. Which two statements does the course support? (Select two.)

options.a: It matters only if the email carries an attachment or a link
options.b: It is a formality that was settled when the task began
options.c: It is low risk now that classifiers screen the actions
options.d: Approving unread hands approval to whatever was injected
options.e: Reading it is the moment a planted request can be caught

explanation.d: The confirmation prompt is the control: content Claude read can plant a request such as this send, and reading the confirmation is where it is caught, so the habit is to "read each confirmation before agreeing" (module 10, page 2).
explanation.e: The confirmation prompt is the control: content Claude read can plant a request such as this send, and reading the confirmation is where it is caught, so the habit is to "read each confirmation before agreeing" (module 10, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says to "Use Manual approval for sending, deleting, buying and posting", whatever the email carries.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Do not press Allow out of habit".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the risk is not zero".

quizzes.stem: A team lead tags Claude in a public channel and asks it to summarise what the finance team said in their private channel. What will happen?

options.a: It reads it through the lead's own membership
options.b: It searches the private room as a person would
options.c: It works from a canvas posted in the public room
options.d: It cannot read that room from outside it

explanation.d: Claude Tag reads other public channels only by searching, and private channels and DMs only from inside them (module 8, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Private channels and DMs are read only from inside them", whoever tags it.
explanation.b: Ruled out because search reaches only "other public channels only by searching, as a person would".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A Slack canvas is not readable".

quizzes.stem: A campaign group plans to have Claude send thousands of personal-looking messages to voters that hide their automated origin. Which prohibited category on the policy's list fits?

options.a: Abusing the platform, such as evading a ban
options.b: Criminal-justice, censorship and surveillance uses
options.c: Undermining democratic processes, such as deceptive content
options.d: Fraudulent, abusive or predatory practices aimed at customers

explanation.c: The policy lists undermining democratic processes, such as deceptive political content or automated messages that hide their artificial origin (module 10, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because that category covers "evading a ban through another account or deliberately bypassing guardrails".
explanation.b: Ruled out because that category covers "tracking a person's location without consent or scoring people's trustworthiness".
explanation.d: Ruled out because that category lists "phishing, fake reviews, falsified documents".

quizzes.stem: A consultant sends a client a market summary drafted with Claude, and the client's own policy asks suppliers to say when AI helped. The consultant says nothing. Which responsibility was skipped?

options.a: Data care, such as keeping client files out of the chat
options.b: Accountability for the accuracy of what is sent to the client
options.c: Fairness and impact on the people the summary covers
options.d: Honesty with recipients about the tool's part in the work

explanation.d: Disclosure: be honest about the AI's part when it matters to them, when a policy requires it or when they ask (module 5, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Do not put in what you may not share; anonymise first".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "An error in AI-assisted work is your error to correct".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the duty is to "Consider who is affected by the work".

quizzes.stem: A company builds an autonomous assistant that acts for customers, with no person reading each output, and its lawyer is drafting the compliance plan. Which scope of the Usage Policy should the plan cover?

options.a: The high-risk requirements alone, for the customers it advises
options.b: The universal standards, plus the added guidelines for agentic use
options.c: The rules for whoever later reads its output, not the system itself
options.d: The additional guidelines for agents alone, in place of the standards

explanation.b: The policy has universal standards, high-risk requirements and additional guidelines for chatbots, minors, agentic use and MCP servers, and agentic use must still comply (module 10, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the high-risk requirements are "for consumer-facing uses in sensitive fields", alongside the standards for everyone.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "agentic use must still comply with the policy".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the policy has "universal usage standards that apply to everyone".

quizzes.stem: A researcher uses Research mode all morning and then finds the usage limits nearly exhausted, though ordinary chats were few. What explains it?

options.a: Research runs on the free plan, which gives a smaller allowance than paid chat
options.b: Memory was switched on, which re-reads every earlier chat each time it answers
options.c: Research runs a larger model whose use counts several times over
options.d: It retrieves many sources, which drains allowances faster than simple talk

explanation.d: Research counts against the same limits as ordinary chat but can use them up faster because it retrieves many sources (module 7, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because Research "needs a paid plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise)".
explanation.b: Ruled out because memory "holds preferences and context that Claude picked up" and does not re-read old chats.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Research counts against the same limits as ordinary chat", and the page puts the faster use down to the sources it retrieves.

quizzes.stem: A multi-turn assistant on Claude Opus 5.5 with thinking active fills its window sooner than the team expected, though visible replies are short. What contributes?

options.a: Older turns are trimmed from each request, so history stops adding up
options.b: Earlier reasoning stays by default, so each request carries more of it
options.c: Thinking is billed as output, so it adds cost but takes no window space
options.d: Token counts are estimates, so the window looks fuller than it really is

explanation.b: Thinking tokens count toward the context window, and current Opus, Sonnet and Fable models keep earlier thinking by default (module 4, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because each turn's input is "all previous conversation history plus the current user message".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Thinking tokens count toward the context window".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a token count is an estimate that "might differ by a small amount", while the window fills for real.

quizzes.stem: On a Team plan, an analyst's Excel conversation cannot write into the open Word memo, though the add-in works fine in each app. What is the likeliest cause?

options.a: The cross-file setting is off by default there, and set per device
options.b: Excel instructions carry into Word, so the two sets must have conflicted
options.c: Claude can open and switch files itself, so the memo must have been locked
options.d: Word memos can be read by Claude only through a cloud platform

explanation.a: "Let Claude work across files" is off by default for Team and Enterprise, on by default for Pro and Max, and set per device (module 8, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because a formatting convention "does not carry into Word or PowerPoint".
explanation.c: Ruled out because it "cannot open, create or switch files itself".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Cross-app work is not supported through Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure AI Foundry or an LLM gateway".

quizzes.stem: A nightly job that summarised last month's reports now fails with a "prompt is too long" error on this month's larger reports, using the same code. Which statement fits?

options.a: Raising the output limit enlarges the window, so the job will then pass
options.b: A newer model accepts an oversized request, so switching lets it run
options.c: The input alone exceeds the window, so it is refused before any output
options.d: First-in, first-out trimming in the API would drop enough to let it fit

explanation.c: Input that alone exceeds the window is refused with a 400 error on every model (module 1, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Raising it does not enlarge the window".
explanation.b: Ruled out because when the input alone exceeds the window "the API returns a 400 invalid_request_error" on every model.
explanation.d: Ruled out because chat products "can manage the window on a rolling first-in, first-out basis; the API does not".

quizzes.stem: A request with thinking active returns an answer cut off mid-sentence, though the output limit was set generously and the input is small. Which two statements explain it? (Select two.)

options.a: The output cap also counts the prompt tokens sent
options.b: Reasoning tokens count against that same cap
options.c: Claude imposes its own word limit on each answer
options.d: Less room is left for the text the reader sees
options.e: Only a short summary of the thinking is counted

explanation.b: Thinking tokens are "billed as output tokens" and leave less room for the visible answer inside max_tokens (module 1, page 1).
explanation.d: Thinking tokens are "billed as output tokens" and leave less room for the visible answer inside max_tokens (module 1, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "max_tokens is a cap on output, not on context".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the loop ends when "the output reaches the max_tokens limit you set", a limit the caller chooses.
explanation.e: Ruled out because reasoning is "billed as output tokens, even when the thinking text isn't returned to you".

quizzes.stem: A summarisation job on Claude Opus 5.5 sends short inputs but generates long answers, and the bill is higher than planned. Which price fact points to the lever?

options.a: Thinking is free on this model, so only the visible output adds cost
options.b: Every token costs $4 a million, so only the prompt length matters
options.c: A produced token costs five times a fed-in one, so trim the replies
options.d: Caching cuts the output price, so caching the prompt saves the most

explanation.c: The table lists Claude Opus 5.5 at $4 input and $20 output per million tokens, so output costs five times as much and shorter answers save the most (module 3, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The tokens Claude spends reasoning are billed as output tokens".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the lineup lists "Price per million tokens, input / output", two prices and not one.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "prompt cache reads cost a fraction of the base input price".
